<div class="nv-rule" id="the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log">

## The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log"><code>packaging/the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log</code></a>
</div>

The registry publishes an **append-only transparency log** of `name → version → digest`: a Merkle
tree with signed checkpoints. Before a client uses an artifact it verifies the artifact's inclusion
in the log and the log's consistency with the newest checkpoint the client has seen. An artifact
absent from the log is refused; a checkpoint inconsistent with a previously seen one is refused and
reported as a registry fork rather than as a network error.

A registry that serves one client different bytes than another must therefore either fork the log —
detected by the next client that checks consistency — or produce a signed statement contradicting
one it already made. Compromising the registry stops being silent, which is the property that
matters; the lockfile ([`packaging/the-lockfile-holds-every-digest`](/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#the-lockfile-holds-every-digest "package.lock records every package's digest, a mismatch is a hard error, and --locked fetches nothing the lock does not name")) then holds the digest so a
client need not trust the registry twice.

The log is also why a registry, rather than git URLs alone, is the transitive source: retraction,
the advisory feed and `nvs audit` all need a namespace with an authority behind it that cannot
quietly rewrite what it said.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Packagist can serve one client different bytes than another with nothing to show for it; here a registry that does so must fork a signed log, which the next consistency check reports</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#the-lockfile-holds-every-digest" title="package.lock records every package's digest, a mismatch is a hard error, and --locked fetches nothing the lock does not name"><code>packaging/the-lockfile-holds-every-digest</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted" title="A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and nvs audit names the minimum bump that clears it"><code>packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#publishing-never-overwrites" title="nvs publish uploads a clean-checkout archive, and the registry never overwrites a published name@version"><code>packaging/publishing-never-overwrites</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0081.md">record 0081</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="publishing-never-overwrites">

## `nvs publish` uploads a clean-checkout archive, and the registry never overwrites a published `name@version`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#publishing-never-overwrites"><code>packaging/publishing-never-overwrites</code></a>
</div>

`nvs publish` uploads a source archive built from a **clean checkout**. The registry requires a
verified account with a second factor, and then:

- **refuses to overwrite a published `name@version` under any circumstance** — a version, once
  published, is immutable; a bad one is retracted
  ([`packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted "A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and nvs audit names the minimum bump that clears it"));
- refuses an archive containing an `nvs.toml` ([`packaging/a-package-cannot-reach-its-host`](/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-package-cannot-reach-its-host "A package ships no nvs.toml, and none of its require or autoload paths reaches outside its own directory")) or
  a git dependency ([`packaging/a-git-dependency-is-root-only`](/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-git-dependency-is-root-only "A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one"));
- records the artifact in the transparency log
  ([`packaging/the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log "The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact")) **before** it is downloadable;
- records the manifest's requested capabilities, so that `nvs add` can show them before a human
  grants anything ([`security/package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time`](/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time "A dependency's authority is granted by the application one line at a time, and a declaration grants nothing")).

Operating the registry — index, artifact store, log, advisory feed, accounts, moderation, uptime —
is a real and permanent responsibility; the protocol is static signed files so that the serving side
is cheap and mirrorable, but the responsibility is the main cost of having a package system at all.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A Packagist release is whatever tag the repository points at and can be moved; here a published version is immutable and is in the transparency log before it is downloadable</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log" title="The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact"><code>packaging/the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-git-dependency-is-root-only" title="A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one"><code>packaging/a-git-dependency-is-root-only</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#a-package-cannot-reach-its-host" title="A package ships no nvs.toml, and none of its require or autoload paths reaches outside its own directory"><code>packaging/a-package-cannot-reach-its-host</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time" title="A dependency's authority is granted by the application one line at a time, and a declaration grants nothing"><code>security/package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0081.md">record 0081</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted">

## A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and `nvs audit` names the minimum bump that clears it

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted"><code>packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted</code></a>
</div>

A publisher marks a version **retracted** with a reason and a fixed-in version. Resolution refuses to
*select* a retracted version and names the fix, while the bytes remain fetchable forever, so an
existing lockfile still builds. Deletion is not offered.

**`nvs audit`** reads the registry's signed advisory feed, reports the minimum bump that clears each
advisory, and exits non-zero for CI. Retraction plus audit is the answer to minimal version
selection's one real weakness — that a patch nobody asked for does not arrive on its own
([`packaging/resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum`](/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum "Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself")) — and it covers the one case a version
range expresses that a minimum cannot: "not 2.3.1, it is broken".

If audit proves insufficient in practice and users sit on known-vulnerable versions, the thing to
argue is a narrowly scoped automatic patch floor, not a general range system.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Packagist lets a publisher delete a release, which breaks every lockfile naming it; here the bytes stay fetchable forever and only selection refuses them</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum" title="Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself"><code>packaging/resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log" title="The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact"><code>packaging/the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0081.md">record 0081</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name">

## A package that breaks its API publishes under a new name carrying `supersedes`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name"><code>packaging/a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name</code></a>
</div>

A package that breaks its API **publishes under a new name** — conventionally the old name with a
numeric suffix, `acme/http` → `acme/http2` — carrying `supersedes = "acme/http"` so that
`nvs outdated` and `nvs audit` can point at it. The two coexist in one graph without conflict,
because they are two packages.

This is what keeps [`packaging/resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum`](/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum "Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself") sound: a minimum is never a
ceiling, so a higher version of one name must always be acceptable, and a version that is not
acceptable is therefore not a version of that name. It is the real cost of having no solver, and it
is paid by the publisher rather than by every consumer. The absorb-don't-forward discipline
([`packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded "A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step")) — Novis's own rule for its Rust
dependencies — is what makes a rename rare enough to live with.

The rule is watched rather than enforced: if library authors route around it by shipping breaks
under the same name, either an API-diff check at publish or a ceiling mechanism becomes necessary.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>2.0.0</code> of the same name is how Composer ships a break; here the break is <code>acme/http2</code>, and the old and new package coexist in one graph without conflict</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/packages/#resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum" title="Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself"><code>packaging/resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded" title="A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step"><code>packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted" title="A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and nvs audit names the minimum bump that clears it"><code>packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0081.md">record 0081</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0">

## Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0"><code>packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0</code></a>
</div>

Two regimes, and the tree is in the first.

**Prototyping — until 0.1.0 ships.** Update anything, at any time, for any reason. Breakage is fixed
in place; there is no classification step, no absorption ladder, no deprecation cycle, no sign-off,
and nothing to write down beyond the commit message. The contract's rules must not be read as "good
practice to start early" — that is how a prototype acquires a compatibility surface it never agreed
to ([`programs/no-compatibility-promise`](/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#no-compatibility-promise "The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp, and no document may promise compatibility")).

**Contract — from the 0.1.0 release onward.** 0.1.0 is the release that first declares the language
complete enough for someone else to write against; which milestone carries it is the plan's to
decide. The switch is thrown once, in the commit that tags 0.1.0, and from then on
[`packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated "A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise"),
[`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot "A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was") and the ladder behind them apply.

The scheme ([`packaging/below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left "One MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left")) and the cadence
([`packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human "Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI")) apply in both regimes. The release tool refuses to
plan a version at or past 0.1.0 without an explicit flag acknowledging that the contract begins
there, and the workspace version is below it.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left" title="One MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left"><code>packaging/below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated" title="A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise"><code>packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human" title="Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI"><code>packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#no-compatibility-promise" title="The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp, and no document may promise compatibility"><code>programs/no-compatibility-promise</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tools/nv/cmd/release.ts"><code>tools/nv/cmd/release.ts</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml"><code>.github/workflows/release.yml</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated">

## A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated"><code>packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated</code></a>
</div>

A version number is meaningless unless the thing it describes is listed. Novis versions **exactly
this**: what parses and what it means; every `Core` member's signature and observable behaviour;
`nvs.toml` keys, their defaults and their changeability classes; the `nvs` CLI's subcommands, flags,
exit codes and machine-readable output; diagnostic *identity* — a code or name an editor, CI or a
suppression comment can key on; the extension ABI a third-party `.nvsx` is compiled against; any
format that outlives the process and can be read back, `serialize()` output above all; and the
supported target platforms and database server versions.

And **explicitly does not version**:

- **The Rust APIs of the `nvs-*` crates.** They share the workspace number as a build convenience
  and carry no stability promise whatsoever; a Rust program depending on `nvs-hir` depends on an
  internal.
- **Anything regenerable from source.** The on-disk artifact cache is self-describing and a format
  change is a cache miss by construction — never a break, never a version event. The same holds for
  a portable bundle, which carries the host that reads it ([`programs/bundle-trust-domain`](/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#bundle-trust-domain "A bundled executable is one trust domain: a program, never a service")).
- **Exact diagnostic prose, timing figures, or the byte layout of anything not listed above.**
  Wording improves between patches.
- **The minimum supported Rust version.** Users receive a binary; MSRV is a build-from-source fact,
  announced in release notes and never a break.

The contract is not in force until [`packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0 "Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0") throws its
switch.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot" title="A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was"><code>packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0" title="Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0"><code>packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#bundle-trust-domain" title="A bundled executable is one trust domain: a program, never a service"><code>programs/bundle-trust-domain</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-artifact-cache/#an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file" title="A compiled unit is one immutable file whose address is its content and its environment"><code>packaging/an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host" title="nvs build --compile appends a program to a copy of the nvs binary, and rebundling is running it again"><code>packaging/nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0042.md">record 0042</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0048.md">record 0048</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left">

## One `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left"><code>packaging/below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left</code></a>
</div>

`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, **one number for the whole workspace**, and the number `nvs --version` prints
*is* the language version. Before 1.0 the breaking slot moves left by one: `0.MINOR` carries breaking
changes and `0.MINOR.PATCH` is always compatible — standard practice, and the only 0.x deviation from
SemVer.

The consequence for anything that assumes plain SemVer is that below 1.0 there is no slot left for a
compatible feature to differ from a fix in, so a "minor" and a "patch" bump agree; and a floating
container tag must never follow `0.0 → 0.1` straight across a break, so there is no bare-major tag
until there is a major. The compatible line is always `MAJOR.MINOR`, and `MAJOR` alone is a tag only
where `MAJOR` is the breaking slot.

The scheme applies in both of [`packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0 "Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0")'s regimes; what
a slot *promises* is the contract's, through [`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot "A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was").

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>PHP numbers a runtime that programs then target; here <code>nvs --version</code> is the language version, and <code>0.MINOR</code> rather than <code>MAJOR</code> is what carries a break until 1.0</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0" title="Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0"><code>packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot" title="A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was"><code>packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tools/nv/cmd/release.ts"><code>tools/nv/cmd/release.ts</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml"><code>.github/workflows/release.yml</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot">

## A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot"><code>packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot</code></a>
</div>

One question classifies a change a dependency forced: **who can see it?** Not how big the diff was,
not how many crates moved.

| The update changes… | Ships as |
|---|---|
| Only Novis's internals — call sites, an adapter, a data structure, a Rust API | **patch** |
| Novis's behaviour back into agreement with its own spec (a bug fix) | **patch**, and the release note names it |
| Behaviour a program could plausibly have relied on, even though it was wrong | **minor**, with the note |
| Anything additive on the versioned surface — a new `Core` member, config key, CLI flag, diagnostic | **minor** |
| MSRV, a build-time requirement, a CI or developer tool | **patch** — no user of a released binary can observe it |
| A removal, rename or incompatible change anywhere on the versioned surface | **major**, and only after the ladder |
| Dropping a supported runtime platform or database server version | **major** |
| A security fix that necessarily changes observable behaviour | **whatever release ships soonest**, including a patch; the note says plainly what changed |

**The asymmetry is the point.** An internal break is cheap and needs no approval — that is what an
implementation *is*. Reaching for a major because a dependency's Rust API changed is a category
error. The surface the table refers to is [`packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated "A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise"); the
ladder its last rows send a change down is [`packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded "A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step").
Nothing checks the classification; it is addressed to whoever runs the sweep, and the commit message
is where it becomes visible ([`packaging/one-bump-one-commit`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#one-bump-one-commit "Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message")).

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated" title="A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise"><code>packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded" title="A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step"><code>packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left" title="One MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left"><code>packaging/below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#one-bump-one-commit" title="Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message"><code>packaging/one-bump-one-commit</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded">

## A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded"><code>packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded</code></a>
</div>

A dependency change that would land in the last rows of
[`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot "A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was") does not go there directly. Work down this
ladder and stop at the first step that holds; every step above the last is preferable to shipping
the break, and the ladder is not skippable because a lower step looks tidier.

1. **Adapt our call sites.** The default outcome, and usually the whole story.
2. **Absorb it behind an adapter we own.** Diagnostic layout is hand-written precisely so the
   language's UI does not shift when a rendering crate does; widen that pattern rather than
   exporting the change.
3. **Compensate at the boundary** so the Novis-visible behaviour is bit-for-bit what it was — the
   right answer wherever the dependency implements something Novis has *its own* specification for:
   regex semantics, decimal rounding, the SQL type map.
4. **Hold the old version, with an expiry.** Written as `# HOLD (revisit YYYY-MM-DD): reason` on the
   dependency's own line in `[workspace.dependencies]`, or as a dated entry in `deny.toml`'s
   `advisories.ignore` for an advisory that provably does not apply. A hold with no date is a bug in
   the hold, and a hold never covers a live advisory that *does* apply.
5. **Fork or vendor.** We then own its maintenance and security response, it passes `deny.toml` and
   the attribution generator like anything else, and it needs the user's agreement before the commit
   lands.
6. **Replace the dependency**, re-running the admissibility questions for the replacement; a swap
   that quietly admits C into the trusted core is not a swap ([`security/no-ffi`](/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-ffi "No userland mechanism loads native code into the process")).
7. **Ship the break.** Requires all of: the user's explicit agreement, a deprecation cycle where one
   is possible ([`packaging/a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands "A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major")), a migration note
   naming the old spelling and the new one, and a major release to ride on.

Steps 2 and 3 mean carrying adapters with no feature to their name — simplicity of the
implementation spent for compatibility of the program, deliberately. A dependency that repeatedly
forces the ladder is a design problem, not an update problem; the hold dates are the evidence.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>PHP's own minors have broken running applications, and a Composer library forwards its dependencies' breaks as its own; here a dependency-forced break reaches a program author only after adapting, wrapping, compensating, holding, vendoring and replacing have all been tried</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot" title="A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was"><code>packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands" title="A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major"><code>packaging/a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name" title="A package that breaks its API publishes under a new name carrying supersedes"><code>packaging/a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human" title="Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI"><code>packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-ffi" title="No userland mechanism loads native code into the process"><code>security/no-ffi</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/extensions/#a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions" title="A C dependency is admitted under ordinary audit only if attacker-controlled data never reaches it; otherwise it needs an exceptional verification record or is confined to wasm"><code>packaging/a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand" title="The third-party notice is generated from the dependency graph, fails closed, and is never written by hand"><code>packaging/the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004.md">record 0004</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0065.md">record 0065</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/deny.toml"><code>deny.toml</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands">

## A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands"><code>packaging/a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands</code></a>
</div>

Where a deprecation cycle is possible — meaning the old and new behaviour can coexist for one
release — the old spelling survives one **minor** release emitting a **compiler warning that names
its replacement**, and is removed in the next **major**. A warning that does not name the
replacement is not a deprecation, it is an inconvenience.

Where a cycle is impossible — a security fix, or behaviour that cannot be dual-run — the change
ships immediately with a release note that says plainly what changed, on whatever release ships
soonest ([`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot "A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was")'s last row). Silence is never an
option in either case.

This is the seventh step of [`packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded "A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step"), and it
is reached only after the six above it are exhausted.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>PHP's deprecation notices are runtime <code>E_DEPRECATED</code> output a production <code>error_reporting</code> hides; here the warning is the compiler's, and a warning that does not name the replacement is not a deprecation</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded" title="A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step"><code>packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot" title="A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was"><code>packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="a-dependency-move-proves-two-things">

## A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-dependency-move-proves-two-things"><code>packaging/a-dependency-move-proves-two-things</code></a>
</div>

The dependency sweep re-runs a battery whose full order and conditional legs are the sweep
procedure's to state. Two of its rules are not negotiable, and this rule fixes them.

**A guard-test failure in `benches/abi-probe/` is never fixed by editing the threshold.** The guards
encode premises other decisions rest on — no native unwinding through JIT frames, what the sandbox
contains, a coroutine round trip's cost class, the regex engine's linear-time bound. If one fails
after a bump, the decision it names is what gets revisited, and the sweep stops until that is done.
The guards run on all three platforms, on any push that touches a crate whose cost they measure.

**A change to the dependency graph regenerates and commits `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` in the same
commit.** CI fails otherwise, and correctly: the notice is a licence obligation, not a report
([`testing/attribution-is-diffed-in-ci`](/docs/rules/testing/coverage-and-probes/#attribution-is-diffed-in-ci "The third-party notice is committed, and a check fails when the lockfile moved without it")). `cargo deny check` and the attribution generator's
`--check` run on every push that can change their answer, and unconditionally nightly and at release
([`testing/ci-lanes`](/docs/rules/testing/continuous-integration/#ci-lanes "One workflow holds every job, and three lanes decide which of them a run needs")); they are what make a hold, a vendored fork and this rule enforceable
rather than aspirational.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/testing/coverage-and-probes/#attribution-is-diffed-in-ci" title="The third-party notice is committed, and a check fails when the lockfile moved without it"><code>testing/attribution-is-diffed-in-ci</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/testing/continuous-integration/#ci-lanes" title="One workflow holds every job, and three lanes decide which of them a run needs"><code>testing/ci-lanes</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#one-bump-one-commit" title="Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message"><code>packaging/one-bump-one-commit</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human" title="Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI"><code>packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/single-file-builds/#the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand" title="The third-party notice is generated from the dependency graph, fails closed, and is never written by hand"><code>packaging/the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0065.md">record 0065</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0143.md">record 0143</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml"><code>.github/workflows/ci.yml</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tools/nv/cmd/gen-attribution.ts"><code>tools/nv/cmd/gen-attribution.ts</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="one-bump-one-commit">

## Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#one-bump-one-commit"><code>packaging/one-bump-one-commit</code></a>
</div>

Each dependency — or one coherent group that genuinely must move together, such as the `cranelift-*`
crates — gets **its own commit**, with its classification from
[`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot "A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was") in the message: `patch`, `minor` or
`major`.

The whole reason is `git bisect`: a bisect across a release then lands on the bump rather than on a
wall of them, and that is reason enough. Nothing checks the rule; it is addressed to whoever runs the
sweep ([`packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human "Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI")), and the sweep's report is where a violation
becomes visible.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot" title="A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was"><code>packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-move-proves-two-things" title="A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit"><code>packaging/a-dependency-move-proves-two-things</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human" title="Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI"><code>packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human">

## Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human"><code>packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human</code></a>
</div>

Being current is a standing obligation, so it has a schedule. The schedule is a **prompt the user
runs**, and **no agent, loop, cron or CI job ever starts it on its own** — an automated bump would
commit the one class of change whose whole point is that a person weighed it, and would do so on
the day a release is being cut. Automated dependency pull requests are refused for the same reason:
green CI does not decide a change's classification.

| When | What moves |
|---|---|
| Weekly | `cargo update` within the declared ranges — one commit, one battery run |
| Monthly | Semver-incompatible crate bumps, CI action majors, the developer toolchain, and every hold whose date has passed |
| Within one release cycle of a Rust stable release | The pinned toolchain, in its own commit, green on all three platforms |
| Immediately, ahead of any other work | A RUSTSEC advisory or a yanked crate in the tree — the one item that may interrupt a milestone |
| At each release | The whole battery, the attribution file, the callgrind figures, and the PHP oracle version the conformance suite was compared against |
| At a major only | The Rust edition, and any hold that turned out to be permanent |

**A dependency more than one minor behind for over 30 days without a hold record is stale, and stale
is a defect**: it gets a hold with a date and a reason, or it gets updated. Being behind is never a
neutral state, because the alternative is one enormous forced migration under a security deadline.
The cadence applies in both of [`packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0`](/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0 "Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0")'s regimes.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A PHP shop's <code>composer update</code> and the runtime's own upgrade are separate projects on nobody's calendar; here the toolchain, every crate, CI actions and the PHP oracle move on one dated cadence</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded" title="A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step"><code>packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#a-dependency-move-proves-two-things" title="A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit"><code>packaging/a-dependency-move-proves-two-things</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/packaging/the-version-contract/#one-bump-one-commit" title="Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message"><code>packaging/one-bump-one-commit</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/testing/continuous-integration/#ci-lanes" title="One workflow holds every job, and three lanes decide which of them a run needs"><code>testing/ci-lanes</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/testing/measuring-performance/#perf-two-mechanisms" title="A per-PR guard and the historical dashboard are separate measurements, and never one"><code>testing/perf-two-mechanisms</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0068.md">record 0068</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0143.md">record 0143</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0026.md">record 0026</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml"><code>.github/dependabot.yml</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml"><code>.github/workflows/ci.yml</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>
